name: MountComponentServerFacet_OnMountDashToggleChanged
summary: The client tells the mount server facet its dash-toggle setting. A 45-byte record with a 17-byte body: the shared head then ONE strict boolean byte. Same facet, same writer and same reader codec as 0x187f, so the two mount toggles are laid out identically and differ only in their type id.
purpose: Carry the client's mount dash-toggle setting to the mount component. What the server does with it is not measured.

created_when: the mount component pushes its dash-toggle setting
lifecycle.if_absent: the server never learns the client's dash-toggle setting

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 bc 61, i.e. type index 6268 = 0x187c. A client record carries the body at record offset 28: the 8-byte frame head and the 16-byte actor id precede the typed header, so a 17-byte body makes a 45-byte record.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: Measured 16 00 99 18 b0 41 c1 f9 = 0x16009918b041c1f9. First u64 of the shared message head: the sending facet's own local id. The mount client facet's own id, shared with 0x187f - the two mount toggles are two members of one facet.
fields.provenance: corpus-wide scan; the head's first u64 is named in msg.time-sync-to-client.json from FUN_1416c1c40

fields.name: local_actor_id_word0
fields.note: Measured bf 85 31 4b bc 4a 95 1a = 0xbf85314bbc4a951a, the first 8 bytes of the client's own actor id - the same value every other capture carries.
fields.provenance: already earned in msg.time-sync-to-client.json; re-measured here

fields.name: enabled_flag
fields.note: Measured 0x00, leaving nothing over: 16 + 1 = 17 exactly. The reader writes the object's +0x20 byte as a single strict non-zero test and its reader FUN_1425a30b0 rejects any byte at or above 2, so the width and the strictness are both from the codec. What the flag SWITCHES is not measured: only the value 0 was captured, so the field is named for the on/off setting the message name announces, not for an observed behaviour.
fields.provenance: decompile: writer FUN_1425a3070 and its reader FUN_1425a30b0; capture: 0x40_T0x187c_W.bin

evidence.ref: object vtable 0x148235f80, resolved by the name-accessor walk (its +0x08 slot is the name accessor: see the sentence that names the string). Message-object slots, using the convention meanings.md established on 2026-10-29 for 0xf37 and 0xda2, where the MARSHAL thunk 0x1414c0730 is `mov rax,[rdx]; jmp [rax+0x60]`: +0x58 = FUN_1438bb170 is the APPLY handler, which resolves a manager singleton through FUN_1416bd7c0 and copies the value in without ever touching the stream; +0x60 = FUN_1425a3070 is the WRITER, which serializes the body onto the stream; +0x68 = FUN_1425a30b0 is the READER, which deserializes the body off the stream

the shared bool writer FUN_1425a3070 is FUN_1414dbca0() for the shared head, then one raw byte through stream +0x40 from the object's +0x20, written as a strict non-zero test. Its matching reader FUN_1425a30b0 reads one byte and REFUSES anything at or above 2, so a wider or non-boolean reading is excluded by the client's own code. Five unrelated wire types share this writer: 0x101a, 0x101d, 0x10b0, 0x187c and 0x187f
